doc.title: Lisa Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 22, 2021

title: Copyist as proofreader and Ellington for New York City Ballet
summary: Proofreading arrangements and transcribing and orchestrating Ellington pieces for a ballet piece.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Did you ever get — well this would have maybe not been able to happen — a recording of the song in some form which would inform you about the arrangement and whether or not the arranger really — I can’t finish my question. I’m just wondering you know if you heard a recording, perhaps a combo arrangement of something that then became a big band arrangement, might you have heard something in the combo that didn’t seem to be jiving in the arrangement, and then have to bring that up with the arranger?

Yes. A good copyist and, I feel like there’s a lot less copyists around and I feel like the art of copying, I’m really glad to have had Tommy show me the ropes about certain things. Because a good copyist is also a proofreader, so you’re not just writing everything out and then that’s it. Like I think in the classical world that would be a different story, but in the jazz world you were expected to be a proofreader. So yeah, I did some stuff, some Ellington stuff for the New York City Ballet in 2018 and I was given some PDFs of them, so it was like Michelle Dorrance Dance, Michelle Dorrance tap dancing was doing stuff for the New York City Ballet and so it was orchestra plus big band. It was an amazing act. It was pretty amazing. So these — set to choreographed to these Duke Ellington pieces. So I was in charge of part transcribing, part orchestrating. Well actually transcribing and orchestrating, that sort of stuff. So I had to go sometimes to the recordings. I was given certain, you know, PDFs and things published and encountered mistakes. And so I wanted to be delicate about it.
Well sure. You must get almost like a sense of ownership with these things, even if you’re not the original composer. You’re so invested in it.

Oh well sure. I mean my name is at the bottom of everything I send out. And I’m very proud of the work I do. And I get, I do have a website but it’s all been word of mouth. I seem to pretty much always have copying jobs around, I’ve got three on at the moment.
